root_idea.summary: The root centers on being sent forth and extending outward, especially in an easy, unforced manner.
root_idea.development: From easy movement and gradual extension develop the ideas of release, dispatch, successive company, communication, and the messenger who conveys a message.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Form IV verb with extensive independent Quranic usage.
Quranic passive participle used substantively in the distinct expression المُرْسَلَات.
Feminine active participle of the same lexical item مُرْسِل.
Passive-participle citation form, commonly substantivized for those sent.
Independent Quranic noun with messenger and message usages.
Plural of رِسَالَة and the same public lexical entry.

senses.definition: To send, dispatch, or cause someone or something to go or arrive.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for sending prophets, messengers, people, angels, forces, rain, wind, and other things; the construction may express sending down, upon, against, or with a message. Active, passive, and imperative forms occur in the Quran.

senses.definition: To release, let loose, or leave unrestrained; hence, to set or turn something against others.
senses.usage_conditions: A distinct Quranic use in which sending involves releasing or appointing something with power over others, especially in the passage about the devils sent against the unbelievers.

senses.definition: Those sent forth: winds sent forth.
senses.usage_conditions: One interpretation of the feminine plural passive participle in 77:1; the form is used substantively and occurs only in this Quranic expression.

senses.definition: Those sent forth: angels sent forth.
senses.usage_conditions: An alternative interpretation of the same Quranic expression in 77:1.

senses.definition: Those sent forth: horses started successively in a race.
senses.usage_conditions: An alternative interpretation of the same Quranic expression, emphasizing successive release in the racecourse.

senses.definition: One who sends, dispatches, or releases.
senses.usage_conditions: An active participle of أَرْسَلَ, used substantively for a sender and in contexts where sending has the sense of releasing or setting something forth.

senses.definition: One sent; a messenger or emissary dispatched by a sender.
senses.usage_conditions: The passive participle is frequently substantivized in the Quran for messengers, including divinely sent human messengers and other dispatched beings; voice and number are grammatical variants of the same lexical use.

senses.definition: A message or communication conveyed from one party to another.
senses.usage_conditions: In a Quranic construction, especially one discussed in connection with 26:16, رسول may denote the conveyed message rather than its human or angelic bearer.

senses.definition: A messenger: one sent with a message, especially a divinely commissioned prophet or emissary.
senses.usage_conditions: The noun is used for human prophets and for angels or other emissaries; it can be applied with flexible number and gender according to the construction, without creating a separate lexical sense.

senses.definition: A message or communication, especially a divinely entrusted message.
senses.usage_conditions: The singular and plural forms denote a message or messages associated with a messenger or divine commission; number and possessive constructions account for the Quranic variation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become easy in pace, especially of a camel.
To become lank, long, or pendent, especially of hair.
To bring or deliver a message.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported interpretation of the Form I verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Leisurely, measured, and composed utterance or recitation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially used of reading, reciting, or speech without haste.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give milk to young camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative use referring to providing رِسْل, milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exchange messages or letters with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reciprocal construction may concern correspondence about a matter or marriage negotiations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To relieve, assist, follow, or alternate with another in an activity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of shooting, singing, work, or reading and recitation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of sending or dispatching a person, message, letter, or messenger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Verbal noun of Form IV.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of sending forth, releasing, letting loose, or allowing something to take its course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes releasing an animal, bird, arrow, water, ship, or other confined thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of uttering letters, singing, or chanting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of letting something proceed freely.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of making speech, property, or a legacy unrestricted or absolute.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative and legal uses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of letting hair down, lowering it, or making it hang.
Leaving, forsaking, neglecting, or ceasing to assist someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use of letting someone go.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The granting of dominion, authority, or superior power over others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived-noun use associated with appointing or setting something over others.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have abundant milk, or for milk and drink to become plentiful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of people or animals possessing milk-producing herds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become possessors of herds or flocks.
To act gently, deliberately, leisurely, and with calm gravity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of conduct and of proceeding in affairs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To extend the legs and let one's clothing hang loosely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use in riding or sitting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To act as a messenger between people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal or intermediary construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To send messages or messengers to one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reciprocal communication.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To alternate with or follow one another in an activity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially used of singing, the call to prayer, or another performance in which participants take turns.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become loose, slack, or pendent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of things generally and of hair in particular.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To proceed at a gentle, deliberate, or leisurely pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially used of a beast's pace.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remain still and steady.
To behave freely, familiarly, boldly, or presumptuously toward someone, and to confide in him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative interpersonal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For fate or time to make free with people and destroy them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic figurative construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To send camels in successive droves.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The camels are brought to water in groups rather than all at once.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Easy, soft, or gentle in pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to camels; it may also describe light or freely yielding she-camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Soft, lax, or flaccid, especially in the joints or legs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a camel or she-camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lank, long, or pendent, especially of hair.
Having much or long hair on the shanks, of a she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized epithet for a she-camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The legs of a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural-related anatomical usage associated with their length.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Gentleness and an easy, deliberate, or leisurely manner of acting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The phrase على رِسْلِكَ means to act at one's ease or gently.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A company or group proceeding successively after another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of people arriving company by company.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A soft or gentle saying or speech.
Milk, especially fresh or abundant milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may denote milk generally; some lexical discussions distinguish fresh milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Plenty, ease, or abundance of provision.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression contrasting hardship with ease or abundance; the expression is also explained by reference to milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The extremities of a horse's two forelimbs or associated shoulder anatomy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical plural.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A drove, herd, distinct company, or collection, especially of camels, sheep, goats, horses, horsemen, people, or things.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The group may proceed successively; the plural is أَرْسَال.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Animals that have milk.
A young girl who has not yet worn the veil called خِمَار.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct lexical use, not the ordinary plural of رسول.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A soft or delicate condition of life.
Heaviness, sluggishness, laziness, or indolence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person characterized by such heaviness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A means or instrument conveying something, as arrows conceived as messengers of death.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stallion-camel sent among she-camels for breeding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse started together with another in a race.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized racing term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A companion who stands with, follows, or alternates with another in competition, singing, or work.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially one who relieves another by taking up the activity in turn.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wide or ample.
Little in quantity or incomplete.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexicographical correction concerning the description of a thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sweet water.
Easy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical use describing ease of conduct or proceeding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A letter or ordinary written communication.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Distinct from the Quranic use for a divinely entrusted message.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A short treatise, discourse, or written work on a subject.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A small work containing questions, inquiries, or problems of one kind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Apostleship or the apostolic office and function.
A name for the female vulture percnopterus.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed epithet or surname.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain small beast, reptile, or insect.
A manner of treating speech as light, slight, or contemptible.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the idiom ألقى الكلام على رُسَيْلاته.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The two shoulder-blades or the veins associated with them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical term with variant lexical explanations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A transmitted report whose chain of attribution is interrupted, especially one related from a Successor directly from the Prophet without naming the Companion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Technical terminology in hadith and transmission criticism.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A necklace, especially a long necklace falling upon the bosom.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May be a necklace with beads or similar ornaments.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who sends a morsel into his mouth or throws a branch from his hand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agent noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A short or small arrow.
A woman who exchanges messages with men seeking marriage, especially a woman separated from her husband or advanced in age but retaining some youth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized social and marriage-related usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who seeks, courts, or resigns himself to death or slaughter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the idiom مُسْتَرْسِلٌ لِلْمَوْتِ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Hair-specific application is covered by the broader loose or pendent meaning.
Camel-specific pace descriptions are covered by the broader easy or gentle pace meaning.
Plural-form statement without additional lexical meaning.
The unit's explicit easy meaning is represented by the appended Classical meaning.
Editorial correction of a corrupt reading, not stable evidence for this headword.
The lexicological interrupted-chain use is covered by the broader technical meaning.
Editorial pointer to the following paragraph.

cautions: The Quranic expression المُرْسَلَاتِ in 77:1 has several transmitted lexical interpretations—winds, angels, or horses sent successively—and these are kept as distinct senses rather than collapsed.
رَسُول can denote either the bearer of a message or, in a specifically discussed Quranic construction, the conveyed message itself.

Several Classical Arabic entries distinguish ordinary message, written letter, treatise, and apostolic office; only the message sense supported for the Quranic رِسَالَة forms is placed in the Quranic form entry.
The active-participle occurrence count is five because the masculine and feminine QAC groups are merged under the masculine citation form.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The interpretation of the Form I verb رَسِلَ as 'to bring a message' is reported in Lane as an attributed lexicographical inference and is retained as a qualified Classical meaning.
The expression involving رِسْل and نَجْدَة is explained both through milk and through abundance or ease; both materially distinct readings are retained under Classical meanings.
A Lane note concerning رَسِيل as a scout or emissary is explicitly reported as a corrupt reading and is not assigned as stable lexical evidence.
